newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Speculative buying pushes up Shenzhen B shares.
newsitem.headline: Speculative buying pushes up Shenzhen B shares.

text.p: Shenzhen B share index closed up slightly on Monday on speculative buying, with institutions sidelined because of poor market liquidity, brokers said.
The B share index edged up 0.31 points, or 0.34 percent, to 90.31 on turnover of HK$14.38 million, compared with HK$12.42 million on Friday.
Brokers said they expect the index to continue moving around 90 points in sluggish trade in the next few sessions.
Appliance maker Tsann Kuen was the biggest gainer on speculative buying, brokers said. The counter surged HK$0.31, or 14.42 percent, to HK$2.46 on thin volume of 6,400 shares.

Zhonghao jumped HK$0.19, or 11.05 percent, to HK$1.91, with 87,160 shares traded. A company spokesman said on Monday the firm is seeking a 80,000-sq-metre site in Shenzhen to build residential buildings for Hong Kong people, with a total investment of three billion yuan.
Dadonghai traded the most on volume of 548,100 shares and ended up HK$0.03 at HK$1.33.

Refrigerator maker Meran gained HK$0.02 to HK$3.19 on the session's second-most active trade of 467,600 shares. Benelux, the sharpest gainer on Friday, fell HK$0.35, or 11.86 percent, to HK$2.60 on volume of 36,840 shares.

Konka lost HK$0.50, or 7.35 percent, to HK$6.30 on volume of 49,450 shares. The company last week announced that it would make a three-for-10 rights offer at HK$5.85 per rights share to its B shareholders, with the deadline for the issue October 29.
The A share market maintained its upward momentum, rising 17.34 points or 4.64 percent to 391.19. Turnover rose to 14.77 billion yuan from 10.02 billion yuan on Friday.
The composite index surged 15.51 points, or 4.45 percent, to 363.87. Market sentiment remained bullish in the absence of negative news, brokers said.
Yanbian Aodong Pharmaceutical (Group) Co Ltd, which listed 13.60 million A shares and 4.40 million staff shares in Shenzhen on Monday, ended the session at 22.21 yuan.
The A shares were issued at 7.20 yuan per share earlier this month, while the staff shares were offered at one yuan per share in 1993.
Building materials producer Fangda soared 3.81 yuan, or 17.98 percent, to 25.00 yuan due to investor confidence in the firm's earnings this year, brokers said.
